public_rationale: The preprint submitted June 25, 2026 reports growing Codex use during the first half of 2026, but does not establish realized human time savings comparable to major historical labor-saving technologies [e1]. METR’s February 24, 2026 update reports tentative developer speedups, while warning that selection effects and unreliable time measurements limit those estimates [e2]. Neither study establishes the forecast’s eventual achievement or permanently rules it out [e1] [e2]. The forecast remains unresolved.
limitations: Usage growth does not establish net time saved after human supervision, checking, and correction [e1].
METR’s developer results provide neither a reliable estimate of the current productivity effect nor a comparison with major historical labor-saving technologies [e2].
These studies cannot establish permanent persistence or rule out gains from future agent technologies [e1] [e2].

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that agents will persist and eventually deliver widespread time savings comparable in importance and scale to history’s major labor-saving technologies.
The claim covers AI agents generally, without restricting their architecture to LLMs.
Time savings should account for human supervision, checking, and correction. Adoption and task performance alone do not establish time saved.
Eventually supplies no deadline. No finite period of disappointing results can by itself contradict this forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Credible evidence establishes sustained adoption and realized human time savings at a scale comparable to history’s major labor-saving technologies.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Decisive evidence establishes that agents permanently disappear or that the forecast’s eventual achievement is impossible. Temporary abandonment, modest savings, and unsuccessful current systems are insufficient.
